new: A new interface: a top bar with search in it, the search palette (Ctrl K) and every screen redrawn with our own icons
Nine themes, Matcha and Blossom among them, with an illustrated app icon for eight
Wallpapers in both themes: a photo, a GIF or a video
SoundCloud search, with YouTube and SoundCloud songs ranked in one list
Imports from Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic, Google Takeout, XSPF and TXT files, and public Yandex Music playlists, albums and tracks by link
Lyrics made on your computer: every word timed, plain lyrics timed, and lyrics written for songs that have none
SOCKS5 proxies with a login, and a check of each service through the proxy
yt-dlp, Deno and ffmpeg download by themselves on every platform
Last.fm shows the song as now playing, and the Discord status is on by default
Fixes for the Notch on KDE Plasma and per-track loudness normalization, and SQLCipher 4.20

why.why: Every feature, no plan to pick. Nuvo Plus costs nothing, since it does not exist. Liner Plus costs $4 a month, and Mpthree Plus costs 149 ₽ per 30 days and holds Mpthree's equalizer, effects, crossfade, shortcuts and song recognition. Riff is free too.

AGPL-3.0-or-later: read it, build it, fork it and share your fork. Liner's licence forbids public forks and any build that talks to a server other than Liner's. Mpthree publishes no source. Riff is open as well, under MIT.

Your library lives in one file on your machine, so you have no password to forget. Liner keeps your library, playlists and plays on its server under your account, and Mpthree needs an account for Plus. Riff skips the account too.

why.claim: Encrypted, with a way back in.
why.why: Nuvo encrypts your library and its audio cache. If the system keyring goes missing, your 24-word recovery phrase opens it. We found no encrypted library or recovery phrase on the official pages of Liner, Riff or Mpthree.

A ten-band equalizer with twelve presets, speed, pitch and reverb, crossfade, gapless playback and loudness normalization. Mpthree sells its equalizer, speed, reverb and crossfade as Plus. Riff gives you an equalizer, speed, pitch and reverb at no cost.

Nuvo recognizes a song from a file, a link, your microphone or what your computer plays (the last two on Linux), and keeps a history. Mpthree puts recognition in Plus. Liner and Riff do not document it.

why.claim: Lyrics for songs that have none.
why.why: Nuvo listens to the track and times every word on your computer. Liner, Riff and Mpthree describe online lyrics, LRC files and manual offsets.

why.claim: Bring your library as a file.
why.why: Exports from Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic and Google Takeout, Spotify CSV, XSPF and plain text, plus links from Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, SoundCloud and Yandex Music. Riff takes links, Yandex Music among them, and its own JSON file. Liner takes links.
A story of your listening, charts, top lists and drill-downs, which you can export, delete or pause. Liner sends play events to its server for history and recommendations.
SOCKS5 with a login and a connection check for each service, so you see which one your network blocks. Liner's FAQ points you to a VPN.
Liner 0.2.11, Riff 0.7.5 and Mpthree 1.1.0 list no arm64 build for either system. Pear Desktop does ship them.
Moments to mark a spot and jump back, an A-B loop, trims for a song's start and end, romanized lyrics, a dislike button on every song and a reason beside each recommendation.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.text: AppImage, `.deb` or `.rpm`, for x64 and arm64. Nuvo keeps its key in a Secret Service keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet. Without one, the key stays in a file that you can seal with a passphrase in Settings, Application, Storage. On a Chromebook, turn on Linux in the ChromeOS settings and install the `.deb`.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.text: The installer (`.exe`) or the portable `.zip`, for x64 and arm64.

platforms.name: macOS
platforms.text: The `.dmg` for Apple silicon or Intel. We are looking for testers: tell us what works and what breaks in [the chat](https://t.me/getnuvo_chat).

unsigned:
Builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet. A certificate costs money every year and Nuvo is free, so your system may warn you the first time:

- **Windows:** in SmartScreen, choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** open Nuvo once. When macOS blocks it, go to **System Settings**, **Privacy & Security**, and press **Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** make the AppImage executable and run it.

notes: Unknown means we found no source we could cite. It does not mean the app lacks the feature, and it is never counted as a no.
Yes and Partly cells have a source in .github/readme/comparison-sources.json. No cells rest on a repository we read or a limit the product's own docs state.

Liner cells come from its README, docs and website at commit 197179b, and Riff cells from its README at ac68b13 and riff.hs.vc, all read on 2026-11-14. Older cells keep their 2026-11-07 sources. On 2026-11-14 we turned 14 Liner and Riff cells whose earlier source was never recorded into unknown.
Mpthree cells come from mpthree.fun, its tariffs and its terms (in Russian, updated 2026-11-07), read on 2026-11-14. Mpthree Plus costs 149 ₽ per 30 days; features that need Plus are marked Partly.

Spotify, YouTube Music and Apple Music cells come from their help pages, except three cells sourced from SlashGear. Several rows carry over from an earlier pass whose source was not recorded; they are marked in the sources file.

Nuvo cells describe the app on Linux, its main platform. The Windows and macOS builds are the same app, except that MPRIS, the panel widgets and recognition from the microphone or system sound are Linux only. Rows added on 2026-11-08 carry yes for Nuvo and unknown for the others: we did not look for them elsewhere.
The rows are the features of the Nuvo app, so they favour Nuvo by construction. A feature another app has and Nuvo lacks is not listed here.
